messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: hosted-api eu-west surge. Severity: P2. Pager: @maya (eng-oncall). Auto-annotations: queue_growth, autoscale_fail, possible-quota.

maya: noticed p95->p99 spike and queued requests climbing fast (12k -> 84k in 7m). dashboards: hosted-queue.eu-west backlog chart.

john: looking at provisioner logs — autoscaler started 6 attempts to create GPU instances; 3 succeeded, 3 failed with QuotaExceeded. error snippet: `CreateNodeGroup: error: quotaExceeded (gpus-per-region)`

sophie: we also have two failed AZ placements — provisioner retried to same AZ and hit thin-pool fragmentation. logs: `instance create timeout -> rollback` repeated.

maya: immediate mitigations: 1) enable fallback routing to ded-1 (dedicated pool) for high-latency requests; 2) apply temporary rate-limit per-tenant at edge for top 5 noisy tenants; 3) scale down model size via routing (switch some calls to gpt-small-ql4 where acceptable). I can run (1) and (2) now.

carlos: on it — kicking failover to ded-1. Running `curl -X POST https://ops-api/reroute -d '{"route":"ded-1","selector":"hosted:eu-west","weight":20}'`  — will monitor.

john: reprovisioner still seeing quota errors. Reach out to cloud quota escalation? We might exhaust region-level GPU quota, need a temporary soft-limit bump. I can ping infra-cc.

ops-lead: I'm opening an urgent quota ticket now (cloud case #CC-2026-3456). ETA from cloud is unknown; ask sales to notify impacted enterprise customers?

maya: applied edge rate-limits: `x-rate-limit: 60rps` for top noisy customers, enabled backend prioritization for low-latency routes. Starting to see queue growth rate slow.

sophie: ded-1 accepted some traffic, success rate ~70% for rerouted requests. Need to watch tail latency — some requests still hit hosted and time out.

john: as a safety, enabling prefix/KV cache for repeated requests for 30m window to reduce token regen. Patch: `config.cache.prefix.enabled=true` rolled.

carlos: cloud support responded: they see quota at limit due to recent partner onboarding — tentative bump in 2h if we can justify. Meanwhile we can spin smaller quantized instances in apac->eu-west host? risky but possible.

maya: customer impact: we saw increased 504s for a subset of customers (approx 0.8% of total requests in eu-west during the spike). Notifying support to surface to affected accounts.

ops-lead: runbook check — are we hitting autoscaler safety caps? If so, we should temporarily relax max_shard_limit to allow more pods. maya/sophie can we toggle to +20%?

sophie: max_shard_limit currently 80 per pool; raising to 96 might help but provisioning still constrained by GPU quota. Doing it anyway to let already-allocated quota be used.

maya: I bumped max_shard_limit to 96 for hosted-eu-west. Observing in the next 2m. Queue ingestion rate dropping by 40% vs peak. p95 trending down from 2200ms -> 850ms. p99 still high at ~6800ms.

john: created a temporary fallback policy to switch low-priority tenants to a lower-cost model: `fallback_policy: {threshold: p95>1s, targets:[gpt-small-ql4]}` — applied.

carlos: cloud case updated: they granted emergency +12 GPUs for 1 hour to unstick provisioning (CC-2026-3456 update). We'll consume those to clear backlog.

maya: great — provisioning those nodes now. Monitoring backlog drain. If p99 stays >5s after 15m, we'll run the degraded-cascade runbook (notify execs + customer comms).

sophie: note — root cause postmortem likely: quota fragmentation + AZ placemenent bug in provisioner that retried with same AZ affinity causing thin-pool fragmentation then quota exhaustion. Will open PR to change retry AZ selection.

maya: current status (T+22m): queue down to 9k, p95 420ms, p99 1.2s, 504s trending down. Cloud GPUs joined and ded-1 failover helped. Continuing to monitor; will hand off to morning shift unless we see regressions.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: severity reduced to P3. Next: postmortem owner = sophie, timeline captured, customer comm owner = carlos.

maya: handing off to @sophie for postmortem and long-term fixes. If anything spikes, page me. :thumbsup:
